retained_uncited_units.text: The Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) regularly reviews its operational processes and guidance to ensure their efficiency without compromising investor interests and protection.

The SFC has further streamlined measures for processing certain post-authorisation matters for UCITS funds1, following its review and engagement with market participants. These measures aim at facilitating UCITS funds in implementing changes that are subject to their home regulator’s supervision, and will take immediate effect.
Further streamlined measures for UCITS funds
(i)        Change of key operators – Removing the SFC’s requirement on prior approval for change of depository and investment delegates which are under the home regulator’s supervision.
(iii)      Post-authorisation notifications – To align the SFC’s notification requirements with the fund’s home jurisdiction requirements, including the notice periods and content requirements.

The SFC has updated and published on its website relevant FAQs2 , including a revamped FAQ on SFC Authorization of UCITS Funds to facilitate UCITS fund managers in navigating post-authorisation compliance matters, as well as related forms and checklists3 .
Should you wish to clarify any aspects of this circular, please contact the relevant case officers in charge.

units.text: The Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) regularly reviews its operational processes and guidance to ensure their efficiency without compromising investor interests and protection.

The SFC has further streamlined measures for processing certain post-authorisation matters for UCITS funds1, following its review and engagement with market participants. These measures aim at facilitating UCITS funds in implementing changes that are subject to their home regulator’s supervision, and will take immediate effect.
Further streamlined measures for UCITS funds
The key streamlined measures cover the following post-authorisation matters:
(i)        Change of key operators – Removing the SFC’s requirement on prior approval for change of depository and investment delegates which are under the home regulator’s supervision.

(ii)       Material changes in investment objectives, policies and restrictions – Removing the SFC’s requirement on prior approval for material changes in investment objectives, policies and restrictions which comply with the fund’s home jurisdiction requirements, except for changes that involve novel or complex product features and/or which may have local policy implications.
(iii)      Post-authorisation notifications – To align the SFC’s notification requirements with the fund’s home jurisdiction requirements, including the notice periods and content requirements.

The SFC has updated and published on its website relevant FAQs2 , including a revamped FAQ on SFC Authorization of UCITS Funds to facilitate UCITS fund managers in navigating post-authorisation compliance matters, as well as related forms and checklists3 .
The streamlined measures set out in the relevant FAQs will take effect on 28 November 2025 (Effective Date).

Existing applications received by the SFC before the Effective Date for which no approval or authorisation has been granted will be processed by the SFC in accordance with the existing approval or authorisation process.

The SFC will continue to conduct post-vetting of scheme changes (including those not subject to the SFC’s prior approval) and related revised documents filed with the SFC. It may make follow-up enquiries and/or take appropriate regulatory actions in case of non-compliance to ensure investor protection.
Should you wish to clarify any aspects of this circular, please contact the relevant case officers in charge.

1 For this circular, UCITS funds means (i) Undertakings for Collective Investment in Transferable Securities (UCITS) domiciled in France, Luxembourg, Ireland and the Netherlands, and (ii) collective investment schemes domiciled in the United Kingdom authorised as UK UCITS.

dimensions.explanation: The SFC removes its specified prior-approval requirement for covered UCITS post-authorisation investment changes. Operator changes and notification alignment are separate measures. Management companies remain exposed to applicable post-vetting arrangements.

Covered funds are UCITS domiciled in France, Luxembourg, Ireland or the Netherlands, and UK-domiciled schemes authorised as UK UCITS. Materiality, novelty, complexity and possible local policy implications lack supplied assessment criteria.

The product-feature and policy exceptions attach to item (ii)'s removal, with novelty, complexity and possible policy implications independently sufficient. The substantive dispute concerns whether application transition additionally defeats relief or preserves only processing. Extending item (ii)'s exceptions across separately numbered items (i) and (iii) lacks sufficient textual support.

Removal is conditional relief from a specified SFC requirement, not unrestricted permission to implement a change. The SFC states that post-vetting will continue and that it may make enquiries or take regulatory action for non-compliance. Failure of relief does not supply a complete affirmative approval-duty rule.

Use the express 28 November 2025 commencement date. Receipt strictly before that date and absence of approval or authorisation identify preserved applications, provisionally assessed at transition. Publication date and the legally relevant assessment event are not supplied.

FAQs, forms, checklists, applicable home-jurisdiction requirements and the existing approval process are needed for full application. The two opaque missing-dependency identifiers cannot reliably be mapped by their order, despite one diagnostic doing so.

Existing applications received by the SFC before the Effective Date for which no approval or authorisation has been granted will be processed by the SFC in accordance with the existing approval or authorisation process.
The streamlined measures set out in the relevant FAQs will take effect on 28 November 2025 (Effective Date).

For this circular, UCITS funds means (i) Undertakings for Collective Investment in Transferable Securities (UCITS) domiciled in France, Luxembourg, Ireland and the Netherlands, and (ii) collective investment schemes domiciled in the United Kingdom authorised as UK UCITS.

readings.distinction: For a substantively qualifying change with a pending pre-Effective-Date application, reading_1 returns false for relief eligibility. This reading instead establishes substantive qualification and preserved processing separately, leaving actual relief availability unresolved. It therefore does not delete the legacy condition and return true for the same control. The strongest uncertainty is the absent rule connecting preserved processing to the continuing approval obligation. The rival is interpretively meaningful but is not a complete competing executable approval rule. A broader attachment of item (ii)'s exceptions to operator changes or notification alignment was tested and rejected as insufficiently supported by the separately numbered provisions.
questions: Does the existing process retain substantive approval requirements, procedural handling, or both for these applications?
Can a qualifying change acquire substantive relief while its existing application still requires formal disposal?
Do the FAQs resolve this separation without requiring an inferred exception?
readings.statement: The transition can be read as governing existing application processing only, while item (ii) independently states substantive relief conditions. On that reading, legacy application history does not itself negate substantive qualification, but the supplied text cannot determine whether the applicant may implement the change without prior approval. The selected control—actual availability of item (ii) relief for that application—remains unformalized because the necessary connecting authority is missing.
